text: Hello, boys and girls, welcome to Daisy's class again.Today, we are going to review Unit 3.In this period, you will have a better understanding of how to complain and respond to complaints.You are going to review the use of adverbs of manner and consolidate how to figure out the opinion and reasons in an argumentative article.Please get your worksheet ready.Think about what we learned in Unit 3.How to read an argumentative article.How to use the passive voice with modal verbs and adverbs of manner.How to make complaints and respond to complaints.How to make predictions before listening and catch the key information.How to express yourself properly when choosing topics.How to write a descriptive article.How to read a classic fairy tale.First, we will review how to complain and respond to complaints.Please move on to Task 1 on your worksheet.Annie is at the customer service of Shopping More.Listen to the conversation and answer the question.You will listen to it twice.Read through the questions quickly.Ready, go.Listen again.I've been waiting at the fitting room for about 15 minutes and I haven't been served.Well, I'm really sorry to hear that.We aim to give better service than that.I will report your incident.Thank you.So much for listening.Let's check.What did Annie complain about?Yes, she has been waiting at the fitting room for 15 minutes without being served.She complained about the poor service.What did the clerk say to apologize?He said, I'm really sorry to hear that.What would the clerk do?He would report her incident.Clear?Good.Please take a look at what we listened to just now and review how to complain and respond to complaints.Excellent for complaining first.Begin the complaint gently.Second, yes, explain why you are upset.How about responding to complaints?First, express concern.Second, remember, apologize.And then, yes, offer a solution.Now, let's move on to the use of adverbs of manner.Read the sentences below.Find the mistakes and correct them.If there is no mistake, write right.You can find the exercise in task two on your worksheet.One minute for you.Let's check the first one.What's the problem?Exactly.We should use an adverb to modify the verb shout.So, impatient should be impatiently.Next.Oh, yes.Hardly is wrong.Here, we should use hard.Number three.Yes, it's right.The last one.French is a noun.We should use an adjective to modify it.So, we should change perfectly to perfect.Let's review the use of adverbs.Make sure you have a clearer understanding.We use adverbs to modify an adjective,a verb, or another adverb, or the whole sentence,expressing a relation of place, time, manner, course, degree, etc.While an adjective is always used to modify a noun,and it tells us how something is.Think about the difference between hard and hardly.When spring comes, I work hard like you.He achieved his goal to be a professional basketball player through hard work.He wore a big hat that covered his head, and you could hardly see his face.Hardly is an adverb, and it has an active meaning.It normally means almost not at all or only just.We use it before the verb.Let's get some practice to consolidate.Please move on to task three on your worksheet.Read the letter and choose the correct word from each pair.Time's up.Dear Natasha,Well, here I am in England.Thank you for your kind letter.You asked me what it's like here.I must say it's pretty good.The language school is very efficiently organized.On the first morning, we had to do a test, which I found rather, yes, hard.However, I got a surprisingly good mark, so I'm in the second class.I didn't talk much at first because I couldn't think of the words quickly enough.But lately, I've become much more fluent.I'm staying with a family who live near the school.They are quite pleasant.Although I don't see much of them because I'm always so busy with my friends from school.I was surprised how easily I made new friends here.They come from different parts of the world, and we have some fascinating discussions.I hope you will be able to join me next term.I'm sure we'll have good fun together.All the best, Annie.Got it?Emma is reading an article, Tigers as Pets, in the school magazine.She is confused about the writer's opinion on having a pet tiger.Can you help her to figure it out?Please move on to task four.You can find the article and the question on your worksheet.You've got two minutes to finish the task.Find the article.大蒜老抽黄酒生抽盐碳酸水盐盐盐盐白糖盐白糖盐盐盐鸡蛋鸡蛋鸡蛋- 这位书记您有没有想好自己的意见?-- 很好!-- 书记认为有个狗狗不太有道理。-- 您在哪里找到这一点?-- 正确,第三个课题的第一个词。-Think about the difference between the way the writer expressed his opinion and the ways Emma and Matt expressed theirs.Yes, sometimes people don't express their opinions directly by usingIn my opinion, I think, in my view, or as far as I'm concerned.People don't always express their opinions at the beginning of the article.Read the first two paragraphs and find out what the numbers tell us.The writer used the numbers to tell us how popular it is in the USA to have a pet tiger.The writer compared the number of pet tigers with the number of wild tigers left.What about $500?Yes, the writer told us the reason why people prefer to keep pet tigers.Let's move on.Read paragraphs 3 and 4 and find out why the writer is against having pet tigers.You can write down the reasons in task 5 on your worksheet.You've got one minute.How many reasons have you found?Yes, two.The first one is great.Caring for tigers is very expensive, difficult, and dangerous.What about the other one?Excellent.Always living in cages makes tigers unhappy.Read paragraph 3 again and think about what the writer wanted to tell us.What do you think?The writer wanted to warn people not to have pet tigers.Yes, the writer wanted to tell us having pet tigers is not that fun.The writer thinks having pet tigers is neither safe nor fun.So you can understand why the writer is against having pet tigers.Think about the structure of the article.First, the writer tells us a phenomenon about the topic by using lots of numbers.Here, phenomenon means 现象。Next, the writer expresses his opinion.After that, the writer presents his reasons with facts.Finally, does the writer draw a conclusion?No, the writer leaves a question for readers to think about.After reading the article, what do you think of having pet tigers?Write down your opinion and give one or two reasons.Move on to task 6 on your worksheet.You've got two minutes to finish it.Let's read Carey's work.He stated a very clear opinion with two good reasons.You can share your ideas with the classmates after class.Carrie's work brings us to the end of Unit 3.We've learned a lot, but we still have something to work on.Practice makes perfect.This is the end of Unit 3.Remember, practice makes perfect.Today's homework.Thank you for watching.
